headline: Local Court Clerk Retires After 40 Years of Selling 'Gold-Plated' Court Stamps That Are Actually Just Decoupage From Old Wedding Invites
body:
Brajesh Mishra, a senior administrative clerk at the district court, announced his retirement yesterday, bringing an end to a four-decade career of selling 'authentic judicial sealers' to frantic litigants that were later discovered to be discarded, gold-leafed wedding invitation cards from 1984. The discovery occurred when a prominent defense attorney noticed that his 'Order of Stay' document featured the embossed names of 'Ramesh & Sunita – Together Forever' underneath the official court stamp.

"I wasn't charging for the paper, I was charging for the aesthetic of urgency," said Mishra, while clearing out his desk of various craft supplies and antique glue pots. "These lawyers are always in such a rush to file their petitions that nobody ever looks closely at the stationery. I once used a 'Happy First Birthday' card for a high-stakes land dispute, and the opposing counsel didn't even notice until the judge asked why the injunction smelled faintly of baby powder and saffron."

Local law firm partners have expressed mixed feelings about the revelation, noting that while the stamps were technically fraudulent, the sheer variety of festive font styles provided a much-needed morale boost during long, grueling court sessions. "It was an institutional quirk, really," noted one senior advocate. "When you see a motion filed with a glitter-flecked 'Wedding Bells' border, it changes the entire atmosphere of the courtroom from hostile to celebratory."
caption: After 40 years, the 'stamp man' is finally hanging up his glue gun. Turns out his legal documents were 100% legitimate, 50% wedding invitation, and 100% festive. #LegalHumor #CourtLife #DelhiDiaries (satire)
igHook: Would you notice if your court documents were printed on a birthday card?
imagePrompt: A cluttered, dimly lit administrative desk in an old courthouse, covered with stacks of dusty legal files, a pair of scissors, a jar of glue, and a few scattered gold-embossed greeting cards.

sourceHeadline.title: 'Fixer lawyers' facilitating bribery of judges; intelligence agencies should pass details to Collegium: Mahesh Jethmalani

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 2 provides a genuinely inventive, specific, and absurd premise—using old wedding invitation cards as official court stamps—that avoids the repetitive and slightly cynical 'bribery menu' trope seen in other entries. It maintains a consistent deadpan tone and achieves a level of charm by centering on the bureaucratic absurdity rather than just corruption.
